candidates.rationale: The reproduced unlink of operational Git locks by filename is fixed: no lock-deletion branch remains; lock names and Git metadata are excluded. Independent open index.lock/packed-refs.lock preserved inode/content despite old timestamps, and competing Git add remained blocked. These tests show lock preservation, not that prior unlink would necessarily corrupt a repository.

baseline.execution: Parent baseline log inspected, not independently rerun against original production.

limitations: Recognition examines 17 bytes, current-Python magic and header flags. It does not prove bytecode correctness, provenance or that a caller has semantic authority over every matching artifact. No marshal body is read or executed by production cleanup.

Descriptor-relative checks reduce substitution/symlink risks but stat/fstat and unlink are not one atomic identity-conditional operation. A concurrent writer can replace a pathname after the final check; no global transaction or hostile-concurrency guarantee is claimed.

Directories, .DS_Store, opaque caches, scratch, different-Python/unknown bytecode, shared/hardlinked/foreign-owned and special files are intentionally preserved. This is a narrower cleanup capability than the former recursive purge.

Entry/depth limits or access errors produce ERROR and a nonzero CLI result; prior successful individual deletions are not rolled back. Reports reflect observed entries/subtrees, not an inventory of contents beneath excluded subtrees.

SCOPED_OK means only that the bounded selected scan recorded no errors. It does not certify overall repository safety, zero entropy, absence of residual data, physical storage reclaimed or any V_A property.

No purge was run on the actual workspace. All databases were explicitly created inside owned temporary fixtures; Git checks operated only in a temporary repository with isolated HOME/system/global configuration. No operator DB, native protected runtime, network, hardware, keys, publication or ATTESTED artifact was involved.

discovery.method: Native graph search/get_code_snippet/trace_path and coverage first; bounded exact-source reads; changed file reindexed asynchronously and completion observed.
discovery.consumer_scope: Script entry point; former verify_va dependency inspected read-only, never executed.
discovery.caveat: Graph coverage is best effort and source hashes are the review anchors.

documentation.supports: Directory-descriptor relative stat/open/unlink semantics and non-following symlink inspection; these interfaces do not expose atomic inode-conditional unlink.
